Romy Eskens is an Assistant Professor in the Ethics Institute at Utrecht University. Her research lies at the intersection of normative ethics, social and political philosophy, and moral psychology. She is currently writing about issues in the ethics of mind, personal relationships, moral address, and degradation and dehumanization.

Before starting in Utrecht, she was a postdoctoral researcher in philosophy at Stockholm University, where she also received her PhD in June 2022. Her PhD work was supervised by Helen Frowe and Gunnar Björnsson, and was based out of the Stockholm Centre for the Ethics of War and Peace.

Prior to the PhD, she obtained a BPhil in Philosophy from the University of Oxford (Balliol College), and a BA in Philosophy and BA in History from Utrecht University. In the Spring of 2020, she was a Visiting Research Scholar at the University of Texas at Austin.
